# Community Rule Column 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QS (Cave 1), Col. 6 | **Condition:** complete

---

**6:1** Furthermore, no man shall bring a charge against his neighbor before the Congregation without first having reproved him before witnesses.

**6:2** In these ways they shall conduct themselves in all their places of residence. Everyone who is found together with another shall defer, the junior to the senior, in work and in property.

**6:3** Together they shall eat, together they shall bless, and together they shall take counsel. In every place where there are ten men of

**6:4** the council of the community, a priest shall not be absent from them. Each man shall sit according to his rank before the priest, and in this order

**6:5** they shall be consulted regarding every matter. When they arrange the table to eat, or prepare the new wine

**6:6** to drink, the priest shall extend his hand first to pronounce the blessing over the first portion of the bread and the new wine.

**6:7** And in the place where the ten are, there shall not be absent a man who studies the Torah day

**6:8** and night, continually, each one relieving his fellow. The Congregation shall keep watch together for a third of every night of

**6:9** the year, to read the Book, to study the Law, and to offer blessings together.

**6:10** This is the rule for the session of the Congregation. Each man shall sit in his designated place: first the priests, second the elders, and then all

**6:11** the rest of the people, each in his assigned place. In the same order they shall be consulted regarding every judgment, every counsel, and every matter

**6:12** that comes before the Congregation, so that each man may offer his knowledge to the council of the community.

**6:13** No man shall interrupt the speech of his neighbor before his brother has finished speaking. Nor shall any man speak

**6:14** out of turn before the one whose rank is inscribed ahead of his own. The man who is called upon shall speak in his turn. And in the session of

**6:15** the Congregation, no man shall speak any word without the permission of the Congregation. And if

**6:16** the man who serves as the Instructor over the Congregation — if any man has something to say to the Congregation

**6:17** but does not hold the position of the one who consults the council of the community, that man shall stand on his feet

**6:18** and say: "I have something to say to the Congregation." If they grant him leave, he shall speak.

**6:19** Any man of Israel who volunteers to join the council of the community:

**6:20** the Instructor who is at the head of the Congregation shall examine him regarding his understanding and his deeds. If he is fit for the discipline,

**6:21** he shall admit him into the covenant to return to the truth and to turn away from all injustice. He shall instruct him in all the ordinances of the community.

**6:22** Afterward, when he comes to stand before the Congregation, all members shall be consulted regarding his case.

**6:23** As the lot determines by the decision of the Congregation, he shall either draw near or withdraw. When he draws near to the council of the community,

**6:24** he shall not touch the pure food of the Congregation until they have examined his spirit and his deeds, and not until he has completed one full year.

**6:25** Nor shall he share in the communal property of the Congregation.

**6:26** When he has completed one year within the community, the Congregation shall deliberate regarding his case — his understanding and his deeds in Torah. If the lot falls to him to advance into the council of the community, by the authority of the priests and the majority of the men of the covenant,

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering of 1QS Column 6. "Congregation" renders ha-rabbim (the Many) as a formal assembly designation. "Instructor" renders mebaqqer. "Pure food" (tohorat) clarified as the community's ritually regulated meals. "New wine" (tirosh) preserved. Rank order (priests, elders, people) reflects Qumran hierarchical structure.*
